author: jackclarkSF
text: @timnitGebru I do agree with the spirit of your question, though, which is that I think we/the AI industry don't have enough of a culture of reflection / talking about failures / investing adequately in a multitude of different views/approaches to AI beyond just pure tech development.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @timnitGebru @math_rachel With regards to diversity, we have just launched the OpenAI scholars program and are going to work really hard to try and make that a success. We're also actively focusing on this in other areas.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @timnitGebru I can't speak for others but I can tell you we think and talk a lot about this internally and our policy work involves frequent meetings between our researchers and policy people to discuss a variety of issues. Some of this is becoming more visible, eg co-authored papers, etc.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @mer__edith I think this is also a very important point! What advice do you have, besides reading things like surveys and also overviews via orgs like AI Now, etc? I do think this notion of "ok, you're building AI for X, here's what you must know!" is valuable. What can we do?

author: jackclarkSF
text: @timnitGebru You can get a sense of some of what we're focused on by reading the congressional testimony from when I spoke in congress recently: https://t.co/QbCeUcXysw. We're also in the (preliminary) stages of growing a policy team. I would love to chat with you if you have time for advice!

author: jackclarkSF
text: @timnitGebru I think this is a great question. We're not doing direct work on algorithms relating to surveillance, etc, as we don't develop this technology and don't have close links to platforms deploying it. We are trying to do policy work on malicious uses, automation, and education.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @andrey_kurenkov @IntuitMachine @jGage718 @mhdempsey @distillpub @gradientpub That's a good point. What I mean is that I view those publications as being somewhat halfway between fundamental primary materials and accessible outputs for policy people, which also tend to be written differently. Think WSJ or NYT op-eds etc.

author: jackclarkSF
text: @andrey_kurenkov @IntuitMachine @jGage718 @mhdempsey @distillpub @gradientpub These are somewhat useful*, but just producing the content isn't enough - you need to make sure that it is being read and interacted with by policymakers, which requires significant (very rewarding and satisfying!) work. *Both of these publications are too technical for policy.
